packages.label: מְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ
packages.reason: These concepts share the same essential nature: they are all faces of מסירת נפש — the act of surrendering oneself entirely to the Holy One. The Rebbe states explicitly that giving charity IS mesirut nefesh (because money = the soul, as one risks one's life to earn it), and that prayer IS a bechina of mesirut nefesh (per the Midrash HaNe'elam: 'for your sake we are killed all day'). מסירת נפש is not a result of prayer or charity — it IS them. They are three expressions of the same essential act of self-surrender. A strong heart (לב חזק) is also the very embodiment of this quality — the Rebbe says that even heroism of soldiers is only from strength of heart, making the courageous heart the structural essence of mesirut nefesh.

merge_notes.reason: The Rebbe states explicitly: 'וְכֵן בִּתְפִלָּה אִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת כִּי עָלֶיךָ הֹרַגְנוּ כָּל הַיּוֹם — הַיְנוּ מְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ'. Prayer requires enormous effort and battle against distracting thoughts — it IS mesirut nefesh, not a product of it.

The Rebbe opens the Torah with: 'שֶׁנּוֹתֵן מָמוֹנוֹ לִצְדָקָה, וְהַמָּמוֹן הוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ, כִּי אֵלָיו הוּא נוֹשֵׂא אֶת נַפְשׁוֹ — נִמְצָא מוֹסֵר נַפְשׁוֹ'. Money is the soul (one risks life to earn it); giving it away is therefore surrendering one's soul. Charity and self-sacrifice share the same essential nature.

The Rebbe concludes: 'גְבוּרָה שֶׁל הַגִּבּוֹרִים, הוּא רַק מֵחֹזֶק וְאֹמֶץ הַלֵּב'. The strong and courageous heart is the root of all heroism and self-sacrifice. It is not an effect of mesirut nefesh — it is its structural essence, the same thing at the level of inner quality.

packages.label: מְנִיעוֹת וְחוֹמוֹת — הַסְּטָרָא אַחְרָא
packages.label_en: Obstacles and Illusory Walls — the Opposing Force
packages.reason: These concepts share the same essential nature: they are all expressions of the opposing force that blocks a person from divine service and from the Tzaddik. The dataset records the explicit bechina: obstacles-seductions-temptations ARE a bechina of walls (חוֹמוֹת) — the illusory walls surrounding the treasury of fear of Heaven. The Ba'al Shem Tov's parable reveals that these walls have no real existence (they are achisat einayim — illusions). The inner dimension of these obstacles is the twisted/spinning heart (לב סחרחר), which is explicitly called a bechina of the bitter servitude in Egypt and the Tikunim's 'be-kushya' — meaning kushyot and kfirut (doubts and heresy) in the heart. The greatest obstacle of all is מניעת המוח — the division of mind and heart from God or the Tzaddik. All these are the same essential force: the klipa that circles the inner point and prevents approach.

merge_notes.reason: Explicitly in the dataset (reference 1046, bechina): 'הַמְּנִיעוֹת וְהַהֲסָתוֹת וּפִתּוּיִים שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת חוֹמוֹת'. The obstacles and seductions ARE a bechina of walls. This is the direct dataset edge.

The Rebbe states: 'הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת לִבִּי סְחַרְחַר — הַיְנוּ שֶׁלִּבּוֹ מְסֻבָּב וּמֻקָּף וּמְעֻקָּם בְּעַקְמוּמִיּוּת וְקֻשְׁיוֹת וּכְפִירוֹת'. The spinning/circling heart IS the state of being surrounded by questions and heresy. They are the same spiritual ailment named from different angles.

The Rebbe identifies מניעת המוח (division of mind from God/Tzaddik) as 'הַמְּנִיעָה הַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁבְּכָל הַמְּנִיעוֹת'. It is the supreme form of all the obstacles — the inner, cognitive dimension of the same blocking force. The external obstacles (walls) have their ultimate expression in this inner obstacle. They share the same essential nature: prevention from approaching the holy inner point.

stats.note: LM2 Torah #46 has only 1 bechina edge in torahData.js (המניעות וההסתות ופתויים ↔ חומות). Both packages were substantially enriched from source text gap analysis. Package 1 (mesirut nefesh) is derived entirely from the source text, where explicit bechina language ('הַיְנוּ מְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ', 'הִיא בְּחִינַת') identifies prayer and charity as bechinas of self-sacrifice.
